merger_description:
Aurizon Network Pty Ltd (**Aurizon**) applied for a notification waiver in respect of various proposed transactions (together, the **Acquisition**) to facilitate the relocation of an 8.5km section of the Goonyella Mainline rail network between Wotonga and Moranbah North Junction, and develop a 10.8km section of new rail infrastructure on adjacent land (**Rail Relocation Project**) within the area of the Moranbah North and Grosvenor coal mining complex in Queensland (**MG Complex**).

The MG Complex is owned by the Moranbah North unincorporated joint venture (**Moranbah North JV**), which is majority owned and operated by Anglo American plc (**Anglo**) via its subsidiaries.

The existing rail corridor passes over a planned longwall mining area at the Moranbah North Mine. To enable the Moranbah North JV to extract the resource underneath the existing rail corridor and mitigate potential adverse impacts on rail infrastructure within the existing rail corridor, a new rail corridor is proposed to be established on adjacent land.

The Acquisition comprises a number of transaction steps required to facilitate the Rail Relocation Project, including various acquisitions of assets, involving Aurizon, Anglo (and/or Dhilmar Ltd, which has agreed to purchase Anglo's interest in the Moranbah North JV from Anglo), the other participants in the Moranbah North JV, and certain government departments of the State of Queensland.

Once established, the relocated rail corridor will be operated by Aurizon for the purpose of transporting coal, including coal produced at the MG Complex.

determination_table_content.details:
Aurizon Network Pty Ltd (Aurizon) applied for a notification waiver in
respect of various proposed transactions to facilitate the relocation
of a section of the Goonyella Mainline rail network between Wotonga
and Moranbah North Junction, and develop a section of new rail
infrastructure on adjacent land (Rail Relocation Project) within the
area of the Moranbah North and Grosvenor coal mining complex in
Queensland (MG Complex), as described in the transaction
documents provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).
The Acquisiton comprises a number of transaction steps required to
facilitate the Rail Relocation Project, including various acquisitions
of assets involving Aurizon, Anglo, the other participants in the
Moranbah North JV, Queensland Treasury Holdings Pty Ltd, and the
Department of Transport and Main Roads of Queensland.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The MG Complex is owned by the Moranbah North unincorporated
joint venture (Moranbah North JV), which is majority owned by Anglo
American plc (Anglo) via its subsidiaries.
The Acquisiton comprises a number of transaction steps required to
facilitate the Rail Relocation Project, including various acquisitions of
assets involving Aurizon, Anglo, the other participants in the
Moranbah North JV, Queensland Treasury Holdings Pty Ltd, and the
Department of Transport and Main Roads of Queensland.
Aurizon is an Australian rail freight operator providing coal haulage
services and bulk rail haulage services in Queensland, New South
Wales, and Western Australia. It also provides rail network services
via the existing rail corridor.
Anglo is a global producer and supplier of a range of commodities,
including metallurgical coal, copper, diamonds, nickel, iron ore, and
manganese. Anglo’s steelmaking coal business comprises coal
mines in the Bowen Basin of Central Queensland that principally
produce metallurgical coal for export from Australia.
The existing rail corridor is approximately 8.5km in length and
passes over a planned longwall mining area at the MG Complex. To
enable the Moranbah North JV to extract the coal resource
underneath the existing rail corridor and mitigate potential adverse
impacts on rail infrastructure within the existing rail corridor, a new
10.8km rail corridor is proposed to be established on adjacent land.
Once established, the relocated rail corridor will be operated by
Aurizon for the purpose of transporting coal, including coal produced
at the MG Complex.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. The Acquisition involves the relocation of an existing
rail corridor from one area within the MG Complex to another, and
would not result in any horizontal consolidation or removal of a
competitor.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
